identificationRemarks: It appears to be the brown-scutum form of B. dorsalis. This form is predominant in India, and which was originally described as B. invadens (Drew et al. 2005). B. invadens was synonymised with B. dorsalis (Schutze et al. 2015). The black scutum form of B. dorsalis is found more in southeast Asia. The characters that match B. dorsalis are: long parallel sided vittae. narrow costal band, very narrow anal streak, T-shape on abdomen, dark tibiae on all legs.
